item.description:

A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*

item.title: Diamond Rio at American Music Theatre — Sun Oct 4, 7:00 PM — American Music Theatre
item.description: Country music trailblazers Diamond Rio have been delivering chart-topping hits and signature harmonies for decades. Formed in the late 1980s, the band made history with their debut single “Meet in the Middle,” becoming the first country group ever to reach No. 1 with a debut release. They quickly followed with a string of hits, including “How Your Love Makes Me Feel,” “One More Day,” “Beautiful Mess,” “Unbelievable,” and “I Believe,” earning a reputation for their rich vocals and exceptional musicianship. With more than 6.8 million albums sold, over a billion global streams, and an impressive run of 20 Top 10 singles, Diamond Rio has remained a constant force in country music. Known for playing every note on their recordings, the band’s artistry extends beyond radio hits to acclaimed instrumental performances and genre-spanning projects, including their Grammy Award-winning Christian album, The Reason. item.title: Manheim Community Farm Show — Mon Oct 5 — Manheim Community Farm Show
item.description:
The Manheim Community Fair, held annually in early October, is a cherished tradition celebrating the agricultural heart of Lancaster County. Since its start in 1954, this fair has focused on education and community fellowship rather than commercial thrills. Hosted at the Manheim Central High School grounds, it features competitive exhibits for livestock, farm crops, and home arts. Visitors enjoy the famous food stands operated by local non-profits, the Children’s Day activities, and the crowning of the Manheim Community Fair Queen. With free admission and a wholesome atmosphere, it remains a premier showcase of “Manheim Pride” and rural heritage. The 2026 Manheim Community Fair is scheduled for October 5 – 9, 2026.

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Oct 6, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Evening Compline — Fri Oct 9, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Oct 8, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

Join us each week as we remember some of the people who shaped the Church through the centuries using readings, scripture, prayers and music! item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Oct 7, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster
